Finally, space-diversity reception is briefly described. This presentation is made on the basis that others who have similar tasks in providing radio-communication over the long paths can benefit from our experience.

Sonselle wat onderskeidelik termies en met laserpulse gerestoureer is, is vervaardig. Die selparameters van die laser-gerestoureerde selle was vergelykbaar met die termles-gerestoureerde selle. Die laserpulsrestourasie kan nog verbeter word en die moontlikheid van beter resultate bestaan. SYNOPSIS Laser pulse annealing of the implanted layer in p-on-n silicon solar cells was investigated. It was found that 12 per cent less energy was needed to manufacture cells compared with conventional thermal annealing. Thermal and laser pulse annealed solar cells were manufactured. The parameters of the laser pulse annealed cells were comparable with the thermal annealed cells. Better results are possible since the laser pulse annealing can be improved.

abstract: What is a contract? The law of contract is a branch of the law of obligation. abstract: There are many people of my generation who have a rather old fashioned attitude towards students and this is mainly that they should get on with the job and stop arguing the point. articleTitle: IEC is stepping up work for the medical world
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: When the IEC Committee for standards covering electrical equipment in medical practice (Technical Committee No. 62) held its first meeting in 1968, the acting Chairman of TC 62, Professor F Wachsmann, stated that ‘radiation protection can be better achieved by one gram of human brains than by a kilogram of lead’. This statement signalled the future direction of TC 62 in preparing standards for radiation equipment used in medical practice. Through the work of medical experts from all corners of the world representing the views of manufacturers, the medical professions, hospital authorities and other interested parties, thirteen standards covering radiation aspects have been issued and have become widely used in the medical world. But the work of TC 62 has not only dealt with radiation — it has been expanded to cover the total needs of medical electrical equipment. Some 20 standards have been issued to date including Publication 601-1, the comprehensive general safety standard thai applies to all types of medical electrical equipment. Work in hand covers some 40 other medical electrical standards. In a soon-to-be-published article in the journal ‘Middle East Health’, Mr Gerrit Gaikhorst, Secretary of IEC Sub-Committee 62A: Common Aspects, expounds the work of his Committee for medical equipment for the patient, operator and equipment, and on the safe application of equipment. The IEC Bulletin presents these extracts from Mr Gaikhorst's article.

abstract: The year 1981 marks several important anniversaries for the electrical world — the 150th anniversary of Michael Faraday's discovery of electromagnetic induction on 29th August 1831; the centenary of the world's first International Electrical Congress in Paris in 1881 where the first inter-national agreement was reached on electrical units; and the 75th anniversary of the constitutive meeting of the IEC in London. abstract: Operation of a petroleum multi-products pipeline poses similar problems to any other business undertaking: how to cut coses, how to exploit capitalised equipment, how to increase the efficiency of the operation, and how to eliminate expensive manual processes. Telecontrol provides the solution to some of these problems but, in turn, raises some problems of its own. This paper describes some of the steps taken to exploit redundant equipment provided for the purpose of increasng the availability of the control system. It also describes some novel approaches to maintaining the outstation equipment and also feedback from the control system to aid management.

abstract: On 17th September 1981 twenty members of the SAIEE visited the Transvaal Observatory. The visit was arranged by the Historical Interest Group in co-operation with the Astronomical Society of Southern Africa. The fact that the visit, which for practical reasons had to be limited to 20 members, was more than three times overbooked, shows that there is real interest for places of historical value. In this rather young country there are many such places but people do not know about them and consequently these are neglected and sometimes destroyed. How many Johannesburgers who see the outside of the Observatory will realise what valuable equipment is inside and that the streets around it, e.g. Innes Road and Gill Street, are named after famous South African astronomers of the 19th century. Surprisingly even, electronic control and recording equipment of the 20th century was observed to work together with the historical telescopes. But before touching on the purport of this viewpoint first in short something about the history of the Observatory. It all started in 1902 when the South African Association for the Advancement of Science asked the Right Hon Lord Milner for the establishment of an observatory at or near Johannesburg for the collection and distribution of meteorological observations in the Transvaal.

articleTitle: The operating duty of distribution surge arresters due to indirect lightning strikes
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper is a theoretical study of the operating duty of surge arresters caused by overvoltages, induced on overhead distribution line, by lightning striking the ground nearby. Particular consideration is given to the surges resulting from multiple-stroke lightning fluhes. It is suggested that a significant fraction of arrester failures may be caused by these multiple component overvoltages because the resulting repeated passage of power-fellow current can exceed the short-term energy absorbing capabilities of the arresters. Recent experimental data obtained on operational distribution lines in South Africa are presented in support of this suggestion.

SYNOPSIS The development of a 50 A I 000 V power rectifier with the aid of ion implantation technique is discussed. The accompanying theory for the rectifier in steady state conditions is discussed briefly. Attention is given, especially to the influence of the planar process on the breakdown voltage, and the influence of the non-linear recombination mechanism on the forward voltage drop. abstract: A CRUCIAL ROLE An electrical engineer, as defined in the Oxford Dictionary, is one skilled in the construction, maintenance, etc of electrical apparatus. But a better definition would be a person who develops and adapts new scientific discoveries for the good of mankind. Therefore the time is fast approaching, if it is not here already, for the electrical engineer and his Institution to take the lead in a field that will affect the structure of society as we know it today. This field is the automation of the office, the electronic office, the office of the future or the less paper office, whichever term one chooses for the developments that are already taking place in the office due to the introduction of electronic technology into the traditional, people intensive, white collar work area.

abstract: As an ordinary man who only dimly discusses the electronic frontiers of broadcasting that you, Sir James, have been exploring for us tonight, but whose professional life has been spent in broadcasting, may I say how impressive and arresting are the insights that you have shared with us? We have received a glimpse of the astounding work that is being done by scientists and technologists; work which gives new dimensions and new capabilities to this business of communication so that broadcasters, politicians, dramatists, philosophers and academics — but not necessarily in that order, can speak to the people, I do not want to cast a shadow on this illuminating talk, but I must confess to a profound fear of what all those people are going to do with your gifts. Even now, the speed at which we can all communicate seems to me only to add to confusions in men's minds. We fill ourselves with myriads of slightly or indeed largely inaccurate impressions of what is going on in the world and in the minds of our fellow human beings.

abstract: Photovoltaic conversion of solar energy can make an imortant contribution in solving the energy problems of the world. The most important theoretical parameters are the energy gap Eg, open circuit voltage V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OC</inf>, short circuit current J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SC</inf>, fill factor FF and the efficiency η. Practical parameters are reflection R, absorption coefficient α, diffusion length L, lifetime τ, recombination, doping, junction depth and cell construction. The aim is to make cheap solar celts (cost less than 50 c per peak watt) with high efficiencies (7 > 10 par cent). Concentrated sunlight can be used as well as novel cell structures. Silicon seems to be the best material for solar cells at present and more particularly polycrystalline silicon and amorphous silicon.

abstract: It was in London, on 26th June 1906, that the preliminary meeting of the IEC was held. Thirty-three delegates from 14 countries were present to discuss the proposed Rules for the Commission which ‘endeavoured to place every country on an absolutely equal footing, to accord each country perfect freedom to arrange the affairs of their respective Local Committees and also to keep the Constitution of the Commission as simple as possible’. The IEC's first Sub-Committee was then formed, with one representative from each country as members, to study the proposed Rules and report back to the Commission the following day.

abstract: On 24th March 1981, the SAIEE held a well attended Workshop, the purpose of which was, to quote the brochure, ‘thoroughly to ventilate the subject of multiple neutral earthing with a view to its adoption as standard practice on low voltage distribution networks in the Republic’. The working paper for the meeting was a draft AMEU Code of Practice, which covers three systems: Multiple Earthed Neutral (MEN) Protective Multiple Earthing (PME) Protective Neutral Bonding (PNB) PNB only applies to a single consumer supplied through his own transformer and was not discussed.

abstract: Introduction As noted in a previous report<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(1)</sup>, the High Voltage Co-ordinating Committee (HVCC) was established by the CSIR some 12 years ago and has as its primary objective the establishment and co-ordination of research and testing facilities in the high voltage field. Since its establishment, the HVCC's areas of concern and activity have been extended to include several diverse aspects of power electrical engineering. It has also developed a unique role as a medium for the voluntary coordination of various national and multi-organisational research projects in the electric power field.

abstract: Steenbras is the first pumped storage installation to be put into service in Africa. The piper deals briefly with the planning aspects of the scheme ie, location of site, scheme size, machine size and operating role. The principal features of the plant and equipment tog ether with the primary and secondary electrical, mechanical and hydraulic systems and the civil works are described.

articleTitle: Broadcasting technology for the 1980s Twenty-Ninth Bernard Price Memorial Lecture
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Broadcasting is a technology based industry which is developing fitter than most industries. The present surge of technological change in broadcasting is based on the transistor and its microelectronic derivatives, integrated circuits and semiconductor stores In particular. The transistor and its derivatives have also made computers practical Broadcasting engineers have applied computer technology to broadcasting and as a result more and more signals are being handled in digital form. Transistor technology makes equipment smaller, lighter, cheaper and more reliable. Digital technology makes signal storage, processing and distribution easier white maintaining the original quality unimpaired. The paper discusses how these developments are likely to affect broadcasting and its reception in the 1980s.

articleTitle: On some characteristics of electrical variable speed drives with electronic switching control
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: After a short review of the development of this type of drive, it is shown how switching converters can be used to obtain conversion from ac to dc and dc to ac, at well at to control output amplitude of voltages. The fundamental relationships between mechanical output speed and electrical input frequency for electric drive machines are given, and related to the different types of machines. Power dissipation in electric machines is illustrated in terms of a general dissipation diagram including electric input at the rotor, stator and mechanical output at the drive shaft. A short review of tome electrical variable speed drives controlled by switching power converters is presented. Electrical variable speed drives with dc machines and armature voltage control by controlled rectifier, with ac machines and frequency control by invertor and with ac induction machines and variable slip control by stator or rotor convertor are evaluated according to criteria of coverage of the speed torque plane, efficiency and losses, harmonic generation and power factor.

abstract: Arthur Robert (Bob) Mullins was born in Komgha in the Eastern Cape on 4th July 1903 and died in Johannesburg on 2nd August 1981. He was educated at St Andrews College, Grahamstown and was a Rhodes Scholar at Trinity College, Oxford from 1923 to 1926. From 1927 to 1933 he was a College Apprentice with Metropolitan-Vickers Electrical Company, Manchester, England and was a member of the Johannesburg Office staff of that company from 1934 to 1936. He was also a staunch member of the Metropolitan-Vickers Overseas Association. In 1936 he was appointed Electrical Engineer to the Union Corporation, a position he held until 1940 when he became Acting Consulting Mechanical and Electrical Engineer. He was the Consulting Mechanical and Electrical Engineer of this Mining Group from 1945 until his retirement in 1967.

abstract: Walter Henry Milton was born on 18th January 1899 and died in Johannesburg on 25th April 1981. He attended the King Edward VII School and obtained a degree in Electrical and Mechanical Engineering in 1920 at the School of Mines and Technology. Johannesburg. Alter graduating he served his pupilage with Metropolitan-Vickers Electrical Company, Manchester, England. He then returned to South Africa where he was responsible for the erection of the first Class 1E locomotives for the SAR. He joined ESCOM in 1926 and rose from Assistant Contracts Engineer to Chief Commercial Engineer, a post he held until his retirement in 1966.
